executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals a multi-threat landscape across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a BSL-3 select agent — has generated repeated epidemiological updates and alerts across the Americas region, representing the highest-priority biosecurity concern given its pandemic potential and zoonotic spillover risk. Concurrent threats include mpox, yellow fever, dengue, and a resurgent pertussis wave in the Americas, alongside the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in late April 2026. The simultaneous circulation of multiple respiratory and vector-borne pathogens across overlapping geographies elevates the cumulative public health burden significantly.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas demands urgent attention as the highest-priority select agent threat, compounded by simultaneous outbreaks of mpox, yellow fever, dengue, and pertussis across the region.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing spread
Zoonotic spillover events reported in the Americas with potential human exposure
BSL-3 select agent with documented human fatality rates exceeding 50% historically
Sustained animal reservoir activity in poultry and wild birds sustaining spillover risk
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce biosafety protocols at poultry operations; ensure stockpiled antiviral availability; prepare pandemic contingency plans

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active transmission
Continued circulation in the Americas following prior global emergency phase
BSL-3 pathogen with expanding geographic footprint in the region
Risk of clade diversification and vaccine coverage gaps
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination; ensure diagnostic capacity in affected countries; monitor for clade Ib importations into the Americas

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 signaling active cases
Sylvatic transmission cycles ongoing with risk of urban spillover
Vaccine-preventable disease with high case fatality in unvaccinated populations
BSL-3 pathogen with epidemic potential in under-vaccinated urban populations
threats.action: Accelerate vaccination campaigns in at-risk zones; enhance entomological surveillance for Aedes aegypti in peri-urban areas; enforce vaccination requirements for travelers

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season Onset)
signals: PAHO alert dated 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere season
Prior alert in December 2025 noting simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation
Risk of co-circulation with H5N1 enabling reassortment events
Healthcare system strain anticipated from dual respiratory virus burden
threats.action: Accelerate seasonal vaccine rollout for Southern Hemisphere; strengthen hospital surge capacity; monitor for unusual severity patterns or novel reassortants

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update 18 February 2026 documenting widespread transmission
Historically high dengue activity across Latin America and Caribbean
Multiple serotypes co-circulating increasing severe dengue risk
Vector populations remain high following La Niña-associated rainfall patterns
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; strengthen clinical case management capacity; monitor serotype shifts that may drive dengue hemorrhagic fever clusters

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO updates in December 2025 and March 2026 indicating resurgence
Waning immunity from acellular vaccine driving inter-epidemic wave
Infants under one year at highest risk for severe outcomes and fatality
Potential for healthcare worker transmission amplifying outbreaks
threats.action: Reinforce maternal Tdap vaccination programs; ensure neonatal cocooning strategies; review booster schedules for adolescents and adults in affected countries

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026
Post-pandemic vaccination gap cohorts remaining susceptible
Risk of importation-driven outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities
Americas region had achieved elimination status now under threat
threats.action: Conduct urgent subnational immunity gap assessments; implement supplemental immunization activities in high-risk municipalities; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026
Co-circulation with dengue complicates clinical diagnosis and case management
New vaccine availability requires rapid deployment planning
Aedes vector abundance driven by climate conditions favors sustained transmission
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance to differentiate from dengue; promote vector control; evaluate deployment of newly approved chikungunya vaccine in high-burden areas

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents have been flagged in this reporting period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a Tier 1 select agent — generated two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025, March 2026) documenting sustained activity in the Americas, with zoonotic spillover risk to humans representing the most critical biosecurity concern. Mpox virus (MPXV), classified BSL-3, remains in active transmission across the Americas as documented by PAHO's April 2026 update. Yellow fever virus, also a BSL-3 pathogen, triggered an epidemiological alert in March 2026. The concurrent activity of three BSL-3 pathogens across overlapping geographies warrants heightened biosurveillance and laboratory capacity reinforcement.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals documented in available report titles; however, pertussis resurgence may reflect vaccine-driven immune evasion rather than antimicrobial resistance — continued macrolide susceptibility monitoring is warranted
Co-circulation of multiple bacterial and viral pathogens increases risk of inappropriate antibiotic prescribing, potentially driving community AMR in resource-limited Americas settings
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen alert fatigue risk: at least 8 concurrent threats across the Americas may overwhelm national health system response capacity
BSL-3 pathogen clustering: three BSL-3 agents (H5N1, MPXV, Yellow fever) concurrently active in overlapping geographic zones in early-to-mid 2026
Southern Hemisphere influenza season starting against backdrop of H5N1 activity raises reassortment surveillance priority
Resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) signal pandemic-era immunization disruption consequences now manifesting as outbreak waves
Climate-driven vector expansion: concurrent dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever alerts suggest Aedes mosquito habitat expansion is amplifying arboviral transmission windows
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (PAHO February 2026) represents a novel non-infectious public health signal potentially diverting clinical resources from infectious disease response
